subject: Clarify product-rights guardrails & feedback license — next steps
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@novum.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greg Hawthorne <g.hawthorne@novumlegal.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novum MSA redlines + product-use question

Ben — attaching the redlines our legal team pushed through (Novum_MSA_redline_v2.docx). Two items we want to highlight for your team before the upcoming procurement review:

1) Output ownership: We need explicit confirmation that outputs generated from our tenant data will be owned by Novum (including derivatives) and that Redwood will not use those outputs to train any public or internal model variants unless we opt in.

2) Feedback/license: We want assurance that feedback (examples, telemetry) submitted to Redwood under the account will not be used to improve models unless we provide an affirmative license and that any aggregated telemetry is anonymized and disclosed.

We have a quick procurement call on Friday. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) accept a customer-first output ownership clause and (b) provide a signed feedback/license toggle?

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Data Platforms
Novum Analytics

Maya — thanks for the redlines and the clear callouts. Looping in Laura (legal) and Aditya (account lead) so we can get an internal alignment before your procurement meeting. Quick notes up front:

- We can discuss an output carveout scope that covers customer content and direct model outputs, but we typically require a limited license for telemetry and aggregated signals to operate the service (health, anonymized usage stats).
- For downstream retraining: our standard approach is opt-in. We can provide a written toggle in the agreement and operational controls for the account (no-training flag) — there are engineering and SLA implications I want Laura to confirm.

Laura — can you advise on the legal language we should propose here (customer ownership + explicit no-train unless opted-in)? Also include any recommended fallback language if product needs some limited anonymized metrics.

Maya / Greg — I propose we aim for a redline response by Wednesday so procurement has time to prep for Friday, but if legal needs extra cycle we'll flag it.

Subject: RE: Novum MSA redlines + product-use question

Ben / Aditya — reviewed Novum's redline set and drafted suggested counter-language. High-level position below; I'll attach a marked draft to the deal workspace.

1) Output ownership:
Proposed Redwood position: We will confirm customer ownership of outputs that solely derive from customer-provided data and prompts ("Customer Outputs"). However, we need to preserve Redwood's right to use non-identifiable, aggregated model improvements. Suggested clause: customer retains title to Customer Outputs; Redwood grants a narrow service license to use Customer Outputs solely to provide the contractual services (deliver, debug, store) and will not use Customer Outputs to train Redwood public models or third-party models without express written opt-in by the customer.

2) Training / telemetry / feedback:
- Operational telemetry (latency, error rates, anonymized token counts) is necessary for platform health. We propose a carveout that permits collection of anonymized, aggregated telemetry and internal model diagnostics that cannot be reverse-engineered to recreate Customer Outputs.
- For any signal that could reasonably contain Customer Outputs (example prompts, flagged chat logs), Redwood will treat that data as potential Customer Data and not use it for model training absent a written opt-in.
- We can add a contract exhibit and an account-level toggle (no-model-training) with documented operational impact (reduced access to some performance-improving routines and slightly higher costs in certain batch paths).

3) Audit & assurances:
We can offer a standard SOC-2 attestation and a quarterly report on anonymized telemetry categories. If Novum needs tighter guarantees (on-prem / Private deployment or Dedicated pools with contractual training restrictions), that is a commercial option and we should scope it separately.

Next steps I recommend:
- Provide the redlined draft language for the MSA and Order Form (I will prepare Novum-ready wording).
- Document the operational implications of the no-training toggle (engineering to sign off on performance/cost tradeoffs).
- Confirm whether Novum requires a Dedicated/Private deployment to meet procurement constraints — if so, route to commercial for pricing.

I'll attach a marked MSA and a short exhibit that implements the opt-in/opt-out flow. Ben / Aditya please review and let me know if you want anything softened before I send to Novum.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Novum MSA redlines + product-use question — proposed language and options

Maya / Greg — following Laura's review, attaching the proposed MSA language and an Order Form exhibit that implements the no-training toggle. Summary of our positions and options below: 

A) Customer Outputs: Redwood will accept a clause confirming Novum retains ownership of outputs derived solely from Novum-provided data and prompts. We will add explicit language that Redwood will not use Customer Outputs to train public models or third parties without written opt-in. (See attached: Novum_MSA_redline_v3.docx)

B) Feedback / telemetry: Redwood will retain the ability to collect anonymized, aggregated telemetry needed for platform health. For anything that reasonably contains or could reconstruct Customer Outputs we will treat as Customer Data and not use it for model training without an opt-in.

C) Operational toggle & options: We can implement an account-level "no-model-training" switch. Tradeoffs: with the switch on, some performance-cost optimizations (certain cross-customer cache improvements, model warm-start paths) will be disabled; expected token-cost delta ~+8–12% for high-concurrency workloads. If Novum requires a stronger contractual guarantee we can price a Dedicated or Private deployment option.

Next steps / asks for Novum:
1) Confirm you want the no-model-training toggle in contract and whether you require it enabled at go-live.
2) Indicate whether you're open to an anonymized telemetry carveout limited to platform health.
3) If Procurement wants a single point of contact for the legal redline review, is Greg or someone else the owner?

I'll upload the marked draft to the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign-ready Order Form once we have alignment. Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call tomorrow to walk through the redlines.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
